agent-roles: micro-plan pair (improvement-eval-agent-open-telemetry + bug-fix-eval-agent) validated the straight-to-impl workflow — brief+impl only, falsification ritual catches the same class of blind-spot that unit tests miss, and combining an observability plan with its downstream bug-fix plan delivers diagnostic tooling + the bug fix in a single arc. Pattern worth lifting into Dusk v2 as a first-class workflow.

rationale-baseline-frontmatter: regex shape risk depends on what the value carries, not the key. Unanchored frontmatter regexes for presence/enum keys (gate_policy, trajectory, workflow, rationale) are low-risk because the value space is bounded; for integer-valued keys they are high-risk because any \d+ substring in any quoted YAML value passes silently. When introducing a new value-bearing key into a file with existing pattern-match parsing, anchor your regex (^...m) even if the siblings aren't anchored — the precedent is wrong for this case. Confirmed by /falsify hypothesis 1 and shipped as 1.25.1 fix-in-scope.

rationale-baseline-frontmatter: falsification ritual value is highest immediately after authoring, not later. Phase 4 of this plan caught a real shipped-to-npm bug ten minutes after the publish that introduced it (1.25.0 → 1.25.1). The cheat-sheet effect is real (author has fresh memory of the code) but the cost of delaying is higher (cold context, lost intuition about seams). Run /falsify on the same session as the impl-complete moment whenever possible. Pattern complements eval-scorecard-format-fix retro's identification of the cheat-sheet effect — same-session ritual catches the bugs the next-day ritual would miss.

rationale-baseline-frontmatter: falsification fixtures must be MINIMAL — any validator rule that fires before the targeted one obscures the test signal. First version of the substring-attack fixture used workflow:feature without OTel/Context/Document gate sections; structural-completeness check fired before rationale-completeness, masking the actual hypothesis. Switched fixture to workflow:bugfix with only the gates that workflow demands. Rule of thumb: pick the workflow with the fewest required gates, include only the minimum sections, and ALWAYS assert stderr contains the specific rule name (not just exitCode) so you know which rule actually fired.

rationale-baseline-frontmatter: TS↔JS parity tests via subprocess are cheap and load-bearing. Pattern (shared fixtures → run TS validator + spawn JS hook → compare pass/fail decisions) worked first try, ~50 lines for production-grade parity coverage between apps/indusk-mcp/src/lib/trajectory/validator.ts and apps/indusk-mcp/hooks/validate-impl-structure.js. CLAUDE.md gotcha already named JS-port-mirrors-TS as a known risk; this plan operationalized parity coverage concretely. Reusable for any future TS-source-with-JS-port mirror in this codebase. The fact that fixtures are subprocess-spawned (not directly imported) means they exercise the actual hook execution path including frontmatter parsing.

rationale-baseline-frontmatter: would have anchored the regex on first authorship rather than waiting for /falsify to surface it. Mirrored the existing file's pattern (gate_policy:, rationale:, trajectory:, workflow: all use unanchored substring matches) without distinguishing that those are presence/enum checks where the value space bounds false-positive risk. The new key is integer-valued so any \d+ substring passes. Author should pre-emptively distinguish between presence-check parsing patterns and value-extraction parsing patterns when adding to a file with established but limited regex conventions.

rationale-baseline-frontmatter: trajectory close audit clean — 0 blocked rows, 0 deferred rows. 8 trajectory rows all in terminal state: T1-T5 + T7-T8 passing, T6 skipped with documented reason (natural smoke deferred to first Numero follow-up plan landing rationale_baseline:1 in its impl frontmatter). admin-ui-hosting: native Node daemon (not Docker) backed by ~/.indusk/projects.json registry; indusk init/update register projects; new `indusk ui start/stop/status` CLI subcommands; route restructure to /p/[project]/...; pre-built Next.js production bundle (variant A3) shipped in indusk-mcp tarball so consumer projects don't need workspace setup; cross-project scorecards view at /scorecards; replaces the broken per-project model in 1.26.0

admin-ui-hosting: 18 assertions covering CLI lifecycle (start/stop/status + double-start guard + port auto-bump), project registry (init/update + collision + stale-entry failure page), multi-project UI (homepage grid, /p/[project]/ scoping, header dropdown, cross-project /scorecards, cwd-aware bare ui), and bundling (zero-extra-tooling fresh install, tarball ≤50MB). 12 end-to-end scripts + 4 manual smokes + 2 tarball-pack assertions. A17 is load-bearing for variant A3 bundling decision.

admin-ui-hosting: chose single long-lived native Node daemon + per-user ~/.indusk/projects.json registry + variant A3 (pre-built Next.js production bundle in indusk-mcp tarball) — rejected per-project dev-server bundled (variant A1), Docker via composable.env (volume mounts can't handle arbitrary project paths), separate @infinitedusky/indusk-admin npm package (version drift), variant A4 source+lifted-deps (no benefit over A3), and lazy npx download (network + cache invalidation). A1 (start <3s) + A17 (zero extra tooling on fresh install) are the load-bearing assertions that lock in A3.

local-telemetry: new InDusk extension bundling Jaeger all-in-one into indusk-infra; env-aware exporter via the standard extension-env pattern (same as dash0) routes dev OTel to localhost:4318 while staging/prod continue to Dash0; MCP tool surface (get_recent_spans, get_trace, get_services, tail_logs) + indusk telemetry CLI give agent + human direct query access to short-term diagnostic buffer — no dashboards, no alerts, no long retention; foundation substrate for the downstream telemetry-watcher-agent plan and diagnosis UX for test-strategy-convention; impl Phase 1 is a hands-on spike producing spike-findings.md that also seeds the watcher brief.

local-telemetry: 22 behavioral assertions + 3 untestable — covers daemon lifecycle (A1–A5 parallel to admin-UI T1–T5), env routing (A6–A8: dev→local, staging/prod→Dash0, zero dev Dash0 traffic), agent query surface (A9–A13 incl. unconditional tail_logs + 500 ms latency budget), CLI (A14–A17), install paths (A18–A20), integration-test diagnosis bridge to test-strategy plan (A21), operational restart (A22); untestable rows U1 (UX feel) / U2 (autonomy aspiration) / U3 (bundle-weight judgment) each with mitigation.

local-telemetry: new InDusk extension + machine-global telemetry daemon (Jaeger all-in-one + OTel Collector + SQLite log sink in a single container image) managed by `indusk telemetry start/stop/restart/status` following the admin-UI 1.27.x pattern — rejected bundling into indusk-infra (couples telemetry lifecycle to graph-infra), custom Collector+SQLite backend (reinvents Jaeger poorly), Grafana/Tempo/Loki/Prom stack (dashboards-first wrong fit), SigNoz/Honeycomb self-host (too heavy), direct-to-Jaeger without Collector (per-service sidecar anti-pattern), skip-logs-in-v1 (cripples diagnosis UX since half of 'why did this fail' is log context), and native-process-no-container (Go binaries don't ship through npm). Chose the extension-plus-daemon shape to give agents direct MCP query access for fast dev-loop diagnosis, with env-driven routing that sends dev traces to localhost:4318 and leaves staging/prod unchanged on Dash0. Container packaging shape (supervisord-single-image vs compose-multi-image) and image distribution (pull-from-registry vs local-build) deliberately deferred to impl Phase 1 spike. Foundation substrate for the downstream telemetry-watcher-agent and test-strategy-convention plans.

Future versions are Dawn V3, Dawn V4, etc. InDusk remains the parent project/company name; Dawn is the v2+ product identity. falsify-phase-authoring: /falsify becomes a phase-authoring action instead of a test-running ritual — investigates the plan, forms hypotheses, appends a new Phase N+1 to impl.md with hypothesis tests as trajectory rows + fix items + standard gates; plan stays in-progress until /work picks up the phase normally. No new phase type, no new validator rules, no admin-UI change. Backwards compatible — existing falsification.md files stay readable and retrospective gate accepts either path. Changes: apps/indusk-mcp/skills/falsify.md + .claude/skills/falsify/SKILL.md (skill behavior) + apps/indusk-docs/src/guide/falsification-ritual.md (docs) + retrospective gate tweak. Library `apps/indusk-mcp/src/lib/falsification/log.ts` kept unchanged. Ships as 1.27.4 patch or bundled into 1.28.0.

falsify-phase-authoring: 6 behavioral assertions + 1 untestable; mostly manual dogfood (skill files are markdown instructions, not executable code); A6 is the one programmatic regression test (legacy falsification.md plans must still pass retrospective gate); U1 untestable UX-quality claim mitigated by organic side-by-side feel across the three pending retros.

admin-ui-hosting: dogfood every rendered surface when a shipped convention changes. /falsify flow shipped in 1.27.4 with admin-UI rendering deferred as out-of-scope; discovered-gap-on-first-view forced two follow-up patches (1.27.6 falsification-rendering + 1.27.7 CollapsibleSection persistence). "Out of scope" for the producer plan effectively means "invisible until someone tries to view it" when the rendering is the only human interface to the artifact.

admin-ui-hosting: quarantine damaged state instead of silently overwriting it. readRegistry originally returned emptyRegistry() on malformed projects.json; next addProject would cleanly overwrite the damaged file with a single-entry registry, destroying all prior entries with no recovery path. Fix: renameSync to .corrupt.{ISO}.bak before returning the default. Surfaced by /falsify T24. Silent fallbacks on read + subsequent writes to the same path = silent data loss hazard. Generalizable beyond registries.

admin-ui-hosting: schedule a falsification dogfood pass BEFORE marking a plan completed. This plan flipped to completed, then /falsify surfaced Phases 8 and 9 as required follow-ups, then we reopened + closed again. Doing the dogfood before the first "completed" flip would have caught those in the normal flow. The /work skill's completion step should include a "dogfood pass" prompt.

indusk-admin-ui: v1→v2 rewrite is a feature pattern, not a bug pattern, when the cost of getting v1 wrong is low. 1.26.0 shipped broken-for-multi-project; admin-ui-hosting fixed it within 24h. Both productive, neither wasted. When the surface is small and blast radius is contained, ship-fast-rewrite beats deliberate-upfront.

indusk-admin-ui: structural detection beats exception-based signaling when the underlying library behaves inconsistently across runtimes. gray-matter throws on malformed YAML in plain Node but silently returns data:{} in vitest — detecting malformed via structural signal (has --- + closing --- + parsed data empty + block non-trivial) is runtime-independent and correct regardless of what gray-matter does on a given day.

indusk-admin-ui: should have asked "what happens when a user has two InDusk projects?" before picking the per-project hosting model for v1. The admin UI is a reader with no per-project mutable state — machine-global daemon was always the right shape. 1.26.0 → 1.27.0 wasn't catastrophic but the per-project lifecycle code is effectively dead weight.
